text:
The National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) was founded on September 22, 1910, by Justo Sierra, with the goal of establishing a secular and national higher education institution, distinct from its 19th-century predecessor. Initially encompassing various city colleges, the university faced early political challenges, including disruptions during the Mexican Revolution. Significant milestones included the first student strike in 1912 and the eventual attainment of autonomy in the mid-1920s following student activism.
UNAM's development included the consolidation into the new, unified campus, Ciudad Universitaria, in the 1950s. The university has been a site of major student mobilization, notably during the 1968 Tlatelolco massacre, and has demonstrated a commitment to academic freedom, as seen in its resistance to socialist education attempts in the 1930s. Today, UNAM is recognized as a research-oriented university, consistently ranked highly in Mexico and internationally, and has actively promoted inclusivity, such as in technology fields since 2016.
